about: Vectors of sealed conversations, docs/sealed.md (version 1). Generated by services/onboarding/tools/sealed_vectors.py; do not edit by hand. Every key here is a test key made from its name. Compare ids and keys as lower-case hex; compare 'devices' in the order of the head roster's device tags. An opened rumor is compared on pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content and the id the opener computes. Signatures were made with fixed auxiliary randomness and only need to verify.
serialisation: A sealed rumor is serialised (docs/sealed.md §4, §8) as compact JSON, no spaces, its keys in the order id, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content, non-ASCII characters and '/' not escaped. The 40 000-byte ceiling counts that exact string as UTF-8 bytes. Every rumor inside a seal here was written that way, and so were the rumors inside a kind 8564's content ({"v":1,"rumors":[…]}, compact as well). An opener never refuses a rumor for its size or its key order.

chains.name: a valid root
chains.note: One device, anchored by the account.

chains.name: a device is added
chains.note: Roster 2 is signed by a device of roster 1 and keeps the letterbox.

chains.name: a device is removed, with a new letterbox
chains.note: Roster 3 drops the laptop and names a letterbox the chain never had. The wraps and keys_handover sections use this chain as alice's.

chains.name: a removal that keeps the old letterbox is invalid
chains.note: Roster 3 drops the laptop but keeps the letterbox: ignored, the chain ends at roster 2.

chains.name: a removal that goes back to an earlier letterbox is invalid
chains.note: Roster 5 drops the laptop again and names the letterbox of rosters 1 and 2.

chains.name: an addition that changes the letterbox is invalid
chains.note: No device left, so the letterbox must stay.

chains.name: the signer is not in the previous roster
chains.note: Someone else's device signs roster 2.

chains.name: a device cannot add itself
chains.note: The laptop signs the roster that adds the laptop.

chains.name: a fork after the anchored path: the lower id wins for now
chains.note: The anchor has no head (= the root). Two valid rosters name roster 1 as prev and neither is anchored yet: the one with the lower id (as lower-case hex) wins provisionally; the other and the roster built on it are ignored. The next anchor settles it.

chains.name: the anchor names the other side of the fork
chains.note: The same rosters; the anchor's head is the roster with the HIGHER id: that branch is the chain, and the roster built on it follows as its tail.

chains.name: ready on the losing side of a fork does not count
chains.note: The anchor has no head; the roster with ready has the higher id.

chains.name: an unknown prev
chains.note: Roster 3 is there but roster 2 is not.

chains.name: only the root the anchor names counts
chains.note: The anchor names the laptop's root (a fresh start): the phone's chain is ignored.

chains.name: the anchor names a root that is not there
chains.note: No chain.

chains.name: a root whose signer is not among its devices
chains.note: No chain.

chains.name: a root with another account in p
chains.note: Alice's anchor names a roster whose p is Bob. No chain.

chains.name: a roster with another account in p
chains.note: Roster 2 has p = Bob.

chains.name: a root with a prev
chains.note: The anchor names a roster with n = 1 and a prev. No chain.

chains.name: ready, then a roster without it: still ready
chains.note: Roster 2 has ready; roster 3 adds a device and has no ready tag.

chains.name: a bad signature
chains.note: Roster 2's signature was changed.

chains.name: an id that is not the event's hash
chains.note: Roster 2's created_at was changed after signing: its id is no longer its hash.

chains.name: an anchor with a bad signature
chains.note: No chain.

chains.name: n skips a number
chains.note: Roster after 1 says n = 3.

chains.name: a device listed twice
chains.note: Roster 2 lists the laptop twice.

chains.name: twenty devices
chains.note: The most a roster holds.

chains.name: more than twenty devices
chains.note: Roster 2 lists 21.

chains.name: no device left
chains.note: Roster 3 lists no device.

chains.name: a device removes itself
chains.note: The laptop signs roster 3 without the laptop: valid, the signer need not stay.

chains.name: a dropped device forks before its removal: ignored, the anchor names the real head
chains.note: Roster 3 (by the phone) drops the laptop. The laptop signs another roster 3 on roster 2 that drops the phone instead; it is a valid step and has the LOWER id. The anchor's head is the phone's roster 3: the laptop's is not on the anchored path and does not descend from its end, so it is ignored whatever its id.

chains.name: the same fork with no head in the anchor yet: the lower id wins for now
chains.note: The same rosters under an anchor with no head (= the root): nothing after the root is anchored, so between the two rosters 3 the lower id wins provisionally, here the laptop's. This lasts until the phone's anchor (it anchors its own roster at once, §3.3), which gives the case above.

chains.name: an unanchored tail after the anchored head
chains.note: The anchor's head is roster 2; roster 3 is published and not anchored yet: accepted.

chains.name: the anchor's head does not descend from the root
chains.note: The head is a roster of another root: the anchored path is the root alone. What follows the root is then taken as an unanchored tail (roster 2).

chains.name: the anchor's head is not there
chains.note: The head names an id no roster has: the root alone, then the unanchored tail.

chains.name: the anchor's head is an invalid roster
chains.note: The head is a roster 3 that drops the laptop and keeps the letterbox (invalid): the anchored path is the root alone; roster 2 follows as an unanchored tail and the invalid roster is ignored.

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor that goes back to an ancestor is ignored
chains.note: This client accepted roster 3 (the phone's) as head. The anchor now names roster 2, an ancestor of it, and the laptop's lower-id roster 3 is there: without the pin the laptop's would win for now; with it the client keeps its head.

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor with no head is going back too
chains.note: The same with an anchor that has no head (= the root, an ancestor of the pinned head).

chains.name: pinned head: an anchor on another branch of the same root is followed
chains.note: This client had accepted the laptop's roster 3 (the lower id, before any anchor). The anchor now names the phone's roster 3, another branch: followed.

chains.name: pinned head: the anchor moved forward
chains.note: Pinned roster 2; the anchor names roster 3, which descends from it: followed.

chains.name: pinned head: a pin this client cannot find is no pin
chains.note: The pinned id is not among the rosters (or is of another root): the anchor decides.

wraps.note: §7: a kind 1301 whose author and seal signer are the belfry's key, to Alice's head letterbox. The belfry has no chain.

wraps.name: the belfry's key does not speak for a member
wraps.note: The belfry's key seals a rumor whose author is Bob: not accepted.

wraps.name: a wrap to an earlier letterbox still opens
wraps.note: §9: sealed to alice_lb1, which is no longer Alice's head; a device that kept the secret opens it.

wraps.name: an id and a sig inside the seal are ignored
wraps.note: The rumor inside carries an id of zeros and a sig: the opener computes the id itself.
wraps.author_chain: a device is removed, with a new letterbox

wraps.name: a seal with a bad signature
wraps.note: The wrap is fine, the seal inside is not signed by its pubkey: it does not open.
wraps.author_chain: a device is removed, with a new letterbox

wraps.name: the belfry's key seals a kind 14 of its own
wraps.note: Author and seal signer are both the belfry's key, but the rumor is a kind 14: the exception is for mail (kind 1301) only. Not accepted.

rumor.content: A message from the belfry itself

history_packing.name: 300 short rumors and one that cannot be shared
history_packing.note: Bob shares 301 rumors with Alice, oldest first: rumor i (0 to 299) is kind 14, created_at T0+i, from alice when i is odd and bob when even, one p tag (the other of the two), content 'Message <i>: "quoted" \ and é' (a double quote, one backslash and a non-ASCII letter: each counts as it is escaped). After rumor 149 comes one more from bob with 39 700 'x' as content: it fits a sealed rumor of its own but no kind 8564, whose JSON would pass the ceiling with it alone, so it is left out. Each 8564 is kind 8564, pubkey bob, created_at T0+800, tags [['p', alice]], content {"v":1,"rumors":[…]} with every rumor, and the 8564 itself, serialised as the 'serialisation' note at the top says. 200 rumors are never reached here: with two 64-character fields each, 200 rumors are already more than 40 000 bytes.

keys_packing.name: a key chain of 600 letterboxes
keys_packing.note: §5.5: the giver's whole chain in several kind 8561 rumors when one would pass the ceiling. Key i (0 to 599) has secret SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/key/many-lb-' + i) and lb = its public key, in that order. Each rumor is kind 8561, pubkey alice_phone, created_at T0+600, tags [['p', alice]], content {"v":1,"account":"<alice>","keys":[{"lb":"…","secret":"…"},…]} in compact JSON, filled until one more key would take the rumor's JSON past 40 000 bytes. Each is wrapped on its own to the receiving device.

ceiling.note: The bytes are those of the exact JSON string that is encrypted in the seal, as UTF-8, serialised as the 'serialisation' note at the top says. The content is described (a string repeated), not written out. For a rumor that fits, seal and wrap were made with the keys alice_phone → bob_lb1 and the fixed values of the case (see 'fixed'), so wrap_id can be reproduced; the lengths are those of the two NIP-44 payloads (base64 characters).

link.note: link = hex HMAC-SHA256(key: the 32 bytes the link secret's 64 hex characters stand for, decoded, not the hex text; message: the 32 bytes of the device's public key).

link.name: a proof made with another secret
link.note: The request's link tag does not match the code this device showed.

link.name: a proof made for another device
link.note: The tag was copied from the tablet's request into the laptop's.

history.note: Bob shares his conversation with Alice to her new letterbox.

an e-mail inside is dropped

history.name: the share's p is not the receiver
history.note: The kind 8564 says p = Mallory although it is sealed to Alice's letterbox: Alice takes nothing from it.

ready.note: sessions = GET /api/me/sessions (only the fields that matter are shown). Counted = chat true and last active less than 30 × 86 400 s before now (last_activity, or created_at when last_activity is null). The roster may carry ready when every counted session's client_pubkey is one of its devices.

cases.name: every chat session is a device
cases.note: Two chat sessions, both in the roster.

cases.name: a chat session that is not a device
cases.note: The tablet signed in two days ago and is not in the roster yet.

cases.name: another app's session never counts
cases.note: A session with chat false is not a device and does not hold ready back.

cases.name: a chat session idle for 31 days does not count
cases.note: The laptop was last active 31 days ago.

cases.name: a chat session active 29 days ago counts
cases.note: Still less than 30 days.

cases.name: exactly 30 days ago does not count
cases.note: last_activity is 30 × 86 400 s before now: not less than 30 days.

cases.name: one second less than 30 days ago counts
cases.note: last_activity is 30 × 86 400 − 1 s before now.

cases.name: a chat session with no client key counts and is no device
cases.note: client_pubkey is null (a session not bound to a key yet), active yesterday.

cases.name: no counted session at all
cases.note: One session of another app and one chat session idle for 40 days: nothing counts, so nothing holds ready back.

cases.name: no session at all
cases.note: An empty list: ready is allowed.

cases.name: a session that was never active counts from its creation
cases.note: last_activity is null and created_at is 2 days ago: it counts, and the tablet is not in the roster.

cases.name: a session never active and created 31 days ago does not count
cases.note: last_activity is null, created_at is 31 days ago.

cases.name: last_activity is what counts when there is one
cases.note: Created 300 days ago, active an hour ago: it counts.

follow.note: A case starts from 'pin' (null: none yet) and runs its 'steps' in order: each is one read (anchor, rosters) given to follow(anchor, rosters, pin) → (chain, pin', event); 'allow_locally' lists devices the person then allows on this device. 'expected' holds the event, the pin after the step (with what was allowed) and the chain followed (same shape as in 'chains'; all null when there is none). A pin is plain JSON: root, head, path (roster ids root → head), anchored (the head was seen as the end of the anchored path), anchored_head (the furthest roster of the path seen so), trusted (null, or the sorted device keys answered without a prompt after a switch), switch_head, prev_root.

cases.name: the first pin, on an anchored head
cases.note: No pin yet. The anchor names roster 2: root and head are pinned, the head seen anchored.

cases.name: the first pin, on a head that is not anchored yet
cases.note: The anchor has no head (= the root); roster 2 follows as an unanchored tail. It is pinned as head, not seen anchored: anchored_head is the root.

cases.name: nothing changed
cases.note: The same anchor and rosters again: the pin stays as it is.

cases.name: the head moved forward
cases.note: The anchor names roster 3, which descends from the pinned head.

cases.name: a pinned tail becomes anchored
cases.note: The pinned head was an unanchored tail; the anchor now names it. The head is the same (event none) and is now seen anchored.

cases.name: an anchor that goes back is ignored
cases.note: Pinned and seen anchored: roster 3. The anchor names roster 2 again: the client keeps roster 3 and its pin.

cases.name: an anchor behind a head that was never anchored is the usual state
cases.note: The pinned head is an unanchored tail and the anchor still names what is before it: the head is kept and nothing is told (event none, not ignored_back: the anchor is not behind anything this client saw anchored).

cases.name: a pinned tail is kept against a sibling with a lower id
cases.note: The pinned head is the phone's roster 3 (anchored); the anchor goes back to roster 2 and the dropped laptop's roster 3 has the lower id: without a pin it would win for now, with it the client keeps its head.

cases.name: a provisional tail gives way silently
cases.note: The pinned head (the phone's roster 3) was only ever an unanchored tail after roster 2. The anchor names the laptop's roster 3 on the same roster 2: followed, nothing told (moved), nobody distrusted.

cases.name: a switch: the anchor leaves a head seen anchored
cases.note: The pinned head (the phone's roster 3, with the tablet) was seen anchored. The anchor names the laptop's roster 3 (with a new device), another branch of the same root: followed and told like a fresh start. trusted = the devices of the head held before that the new head still has (phone, laptop); switch_head = the head followed now.

cases.name: a switch away from an anchored head the pin had moved past
cases.note: Roster 3 was seen anchored; the pin then moved onto roster 4, an unanchored tail. The anchor names the dropped laptop's fork from roster 2, which leaves roster 3 too: a switch, although the pinned head itself was never anchored. Nobody is trusted: no device of the head held is in the new one. (A reading beyond the contract's letter, flagged to its author.)

cases.name: a fresh start
cases.note: The anchor names another root: a new pin, the root held before kept as prev_root, nobody distrusted (trusted null).

cases.name: a pin read back after a restart, then an older anchor
cases.note: The pin comes from storage (plain JSON). The anchor has no head at all: ignored, the pinned head stays.

cases.name: a pin read back after a restart, then a new root
cases.note: The stored pin is one from after a switch (trusted and switch_head set). The anchor names another root: fresh start, trusted and switch_head are cleared.

cases.name: going back while the pinned head's rosters are not there
cases.note: The anchor names an ancestor of the pinned head and the relay did not give the pinned head's roster: nothing to follow (no chain), the pin stays; never the older head.

cases.name: no anchor to follow
cases.note: The anchor's signature is bad: no chain, the pin stays as it is.

cases.name: moved, then the tail is anchored, then on
cases.note: Three reads in a row from no pin: a head-less anchor with roster 2 as tail; the anchor names roster 2; the anchor names roster 3.

trust.note: Who is answered without a prompt (§5.5), mostly after a switch (§3.3). Steps as in 'follow' (the keys alice_new and alice_extra are listed there). After the last step each of 'asks' is a device request: answer_without_prompt(chain, pin, device, live_chat_devices, request_created_at, added_at, last_handover_at). added_at is the created_at of the first roster of the followed chain that has the device (null: not in it).

cases.name: no switch: every device of the head is answered
cases.note: trusted is null. The laptop, in the anchored head, live, asks after it was added.

cases.name: after a switch the newcomer goes through Allow
cases.note: The new device of the head followed at the switch was not in the head held before.

cases.name: after a switch a device held before is answered
cases.note: Phone and laptop were in the head held before and are in the new one.

cases.name: a trusted device adds a device: trusted
cases.note: After the switch the phone (trusted) signs a roster that ADDS one more device: that device is trusted. The newcomer of the switch still is not.

cases.name: a trusted device's roster that only keeps the newcomer vouches for nothing
cases.note: After the switch the phone publishes a roster with the same devices (for ready).

cases.name: the untrusted newcomer adds a third device: neither is trusted
cases.note: After the switch the newcomer signs the roster that adds one more device.

cases.name: dropped after the switch, added back by an untrusted signer: not trusted
cases.note: The phone drops the laptop (new letterbox); the newcomer then adds it back.

cases.name: allowed on this device: trusted
cases.note: After the switch the person taps Allow for the newcomer (allow_locally).

cases.name: chain order, not dates: a descendant dated before the switch head counts
cases.note: The phone's roster that adds a device descends from the switch head but is dated before it (T0+150, the switch head T0+210): it counts.

cases.name: chain order, not dates: a later roster that does not descend from it does not
cases.note: On the branch the anchor left, the phone (trusted) adds the same device, dated later (T0+500). On the followed chain it is the newcomer that adds it. Only the followed chain counts: not trusted.

cases.name: a device the switch left out comes back untrusted
cases.note: The tablet was in the head held before, but not in the head followed at the switch: it is not kept as trusted, so the newcomer adding it back gives it nothing. (trusted at a switch = the devices held before that the new head still has; a reading, flagged to the contract's author.)

cases.name: trusted, but added past the anchored end: not yet
cases.note: The phone's roster adding a device is published and not anchored (the anchor still names the switch head): the device is trusted and in the head, but not on the anchored end.

cases.name: the request must be newer, and the session live
cases.note: The laptop was added by roster 2 (T0+100). A request dated then is not newer; one dated at the last hand-over to it is not newer either; a later one is answered; no live chat session: not answered.

reports.note: The kind 7679 delivery report of a member's outgoing mail, signed by the belfry key, found by its r tag (the mail's email-id), no p tag. content = NIP-44 with conv(secret, the key in ephemeral-pubkey) of a JSON object. With an lb tag the secret is that letterbox's; without, the account's (the signer). 'key_chain' is what the device holds. expected.state: opened (with the body), signer (no lb: not the device's to open), locked (lb not in the key chain: kept), error (does not open with the secret held for its lb). The throwaway key is SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/once/' + the first case's name) and the nonce SHA-256('belfry sealed vectors/nonce/report/' + that name); the third case uses its own name.

cases.name: a report to the sender's head letterbox
cases.note: §7: Alice's chain is ready, so the report of her mail is encrypted to her head letterbox (alice_lb2) and says so in an lb tag. Her device has that secret.

cases.name: the wrong letterbox secret
cases.note: The same report; the key chain pairs alice_lb2 with another secret (alice_lb3's): it does not open.

cases.name: a report without lb is the signer's
cases.note: The old kind: encrypted to Alice's account key, no lb tag. The app hands it to the signer as before and never tries a letterbox secret on it.

cases.name: a report whose lb is not in the key chain
cases.note: The same sealed report on a device that holds only alice_lb1 and alice_lb3: kept, not opened, tried again when keys arrive.
